newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler hit with new car ban in California.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler hit with new car ban in California.

text.p: California's Department of Motor Vehicles Thursday banned Chrysler Corp. from supplying dealers in the state with new vehicles for 45 days as punishment for alleged "Lemon Law" violations.
In a statement, the agency said the ban was reduced from an earlier 60 day suspension recommended by an Administrative Law Judge.

The ban, which is scheduled to take effect in 40 days, prohibits Chrysler from shipping new cars and trucks into the state but it does not prevent dealers from servicing vehicles or selling cars that are already on the lot.

"The action taken today is taken against Chrysler Corporation, not corporation dealerships in California," Department of Motor Vehicles Director Sally Reed said. "Prohibiting the restocking of vehicles for 45 days, coupled with other sanctions, sends the strongest message to Chrysler Corporation, but should have less effect on innocent parties."
The department also banned Chrysler from re-selling so-called "Lemon Law" buybacks and good-will repurchases within the state for three years.

In May, a judge found Chrysler guilty of 116 violations of the state's Lemon Law, including failure to notify used car buyers of the status of vehicles sold, failure to provide warranties and failure to notify the agency of vehicles for which titles must be branded as warranty returns.
